name: ANAND AMRITRAJ
bio:
Career Overview: Playing Style: A skilled serve-and-volley player with a strong net game and consistent groundstrokes, effective on grass and hard courts.
Career-High ATP Singles Ranking: #74 (November 18, 1974), Career-High ATP Doubles Ranking: #14 (March 20, 1978).
Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the third round of Wimbledon (1973) and the US Open (1974).
Notable Achievements: ATP Titles: Won 4 singles titles and 12 doubles titles during the 1970s and 1980s, including the 1976 Indian National Championship. Davis Cup & National Representation: Key member of India’s Davis Cup team from 1968 to 1988, helping reach the finals in 1974 (forfeited vs. South Africa due to apartheid protest) and 1987 (lost to Sweden), with a career record of 34-24.
Other Highlights: Semifinalist in men’s doubles at Wimbledon 1976 with brother Vijay Amritraj. One of three Amritraj brothers (with Vijay and Ashok) who pioneered Indian tennis internationally. Later became a businessman and coach.
Anand retired in the early 1990s, leaving a legacy as a trailblazer for Indian tennis alongside his brothers. 🎾🇮🇳
